title: Bayesian inference and retrodiction for faithful states on von Neumann algebras
abstract: Retrodiction is the act of inferring a cause from its effects, the most common example of which is Bayesian inference. Retrodiction can be defined by its structural process-theoretic properties, which are mathematically captured by category theory. This categorical definition of retrodiction has recently been shown to potentially isolate the Petz recovery map as a unique universal candidate for quantum Bayesian inference. This paper extends these results to the infinite-dimensional setting on von Neumann algebras. In the process, we provide a pedagogical review of the Petz recovery map in infinite dimensions and its relation to the more commonly used expression in the finite-dimensional setting. We formalize the open question as to whether these categorical axioms for retrodiction do in fact uniquely characterize the Petz recovery map. If such a characterization holds, this would show that Bayesian inversion and the Petz recovery map are structural necessities and not simply useful algorithms for classical and quantum inference.
summary: This work mathematically formalizes quantum retrodiction by extending concepts from finite dimensions to infinite-dimensional von Neumann algebras. It uses category theory to show that the Petz recovery map satisfies deep structural axioms, suggesting that quantum Bayesian inference is a structural necessity rather than just an algorithmic tool. This advances the mathematical foundations of quantum information theory.
main_problem: The paper extends the structural definition of retrodiction, typically used in Bayesian inference, from finite-dimensional quantum systems to the infinite-dimensional setting using von Neumann algebras.
main_result: It establishes that the Petz recovery map satisfies functoriality axioms on the category of von Neumann algebras with normal faithful states, suggesting a deep structural necessity for quantum Bayesian inversion.
method: The authors employ category theory to define retrodiction structurally and utilize the Petz recovery map, formalizing concepts like the KMS inner product and functoriality axioms in infinite dimensions.
model_or_system: The mathematical framework involves general von Neumann algebras ($A$) equipped with a normal faithful state ($\omega$), which models quantum systems with potentially infinite degrees of freedom.

important_parameters: The structure depends on the choice of the faithful state $\omega$ and the properties of the modular conjugation operator $J$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is built upon the assumption that the Petz recovery map defines a functor, though the paper leaves open whether this characterization is unique.

paper_structure: The paper first reviews the Petz map in infinite dimensions, then develops the KMS inner product, and finally formalizes the structural axioms of retrodiction using category theory to characterize the Petz map.
why_interesting: It provides a highly abstract, foundational mathematical framework for understanding quantum inference and time-reversal symmetry, connecting it to fundamental algebraic structures.
